name: com.doesitarm/mcp
title: Does It ARM
description: Check Apple Silicon compatibility for Mac apps, games, and Homebrew formulae.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Find Does It ARM listings for a Mac app, game, or Homebrew formula by name, alias, or bundle ID. Returns ranked candidates with reported Apple Silicon status and listing links. Useful when the exact listing is unclear.

query.description: Mac app, game, or Homebrew formula name or alias, or a Mac app bundle ID such as com.spotify.client.

kind.description: Limit results to app (Mac app), game, or homebrew (formula). Defaults to all, which covers all three.

status.description: Filter by reported status. native means native support, rosetta means Rosetta 2, no means unsupported, no-in-progress means support is in progress, and unreported means native support has yet to be reported. Omit to include any status.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked matches to return, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Read one Does It ARM listing for a Mac app, game, Homebrew formula, or Mac model. A Does It ARM listing path or URL identifies the catalog record directly. A name or slug can resolve to the best catalog match. A miss may include suggestions. Details can include app version history, device support, game reports, related videos, or Mac model specifications.

app.description: One listing name, slug, or Does It ARM page path or URL, such as Spotify, /app/spotify, or https://doesitarm.com/app/spotify/.

kind.description: For a name or slug, narrow the lookup to app, game, homebrew (formula), or device (Mac model). Defaults to all, which covers all four. A listing path or URL determines its own kind.

tools.name: check_apps
tools.description: Check reported Apple Silicon compatibility for up to 50 software names in one call, including lists for a Mac migration. Returns the best Does It ARM catalog match, reported status, and listing link for each distinct name. Names without a sufficiently close match are marked as not listed.

names.description: One to 50 software names, one per array item, such as Spotify or Docker. Blank entries are skipped and identical trimmed names are checked once.

kind.description: Limit results to app (Mac app), game, or homebrew (formula). Defaults to all, which covers all three.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Discover the categories available in the Does It ARM catalog. Returns each category’s slug, listing count, and page link, plus compatibility percentages across Mac apps, games, and formulae when available.

tools.name: list_by_category
tools.description: Browse Mac apps, games, or Homebrew formulae in one Does It ARM category. Optionally filter by reported Apple Silicon status. Each page includes listing links and returns the next offset when more results are available.

category.description: Category slug or label, such as music-and-audio-tools or Homebrew.

status.description: Filter by reported status. native means native support, rosetta means Rosetta 2, no means unsupported, no-in-progress means support is in progress, and unreported means native support has yet to be reported. Omit to include any status.

limit.description: Maximum listings per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

offset.description: Number of matching listings to skip. Defaults to 0. For the next page, use nextOffset with the same category and status. A null nextOffset means the last page.

tools.name: recent_updates
tools.description: See the latest dated Mac app compatibility updates in the Does It ARM catalog. Returns Apple Silicon status and listing links, newest update first.

limit.description: Maximum updated app listings to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Find the Apple Silicon Mac models covered by Does It ARM. Returns model names, chips, availability dates when present, and links to the device pages. The listing detail tool can read a selected device page.

tools.name: check_inventory
tools.description: Check Apple Silicon compatibility for installed Mac apps from Jamf Pro, Iru Prism, Intune, Fleet, JumpCloud, MunkiReport, or system_profiler exports, or from up to 250 app-only rows. Raw exports are grouped by app, version and build and return device counts where available. Results include paged verdicts and evidence from version-scoped catalog statements and the ten most recent scanned versions per bundle ID. Name-only matches remain unknown and include a catalog hint where available.

rows.description: App-only input, 1 to 250 rows with a nonblank name or bundle_id. Mutually exclusive with csv and json.

name.description: App name as shown in the inventory, such as Slack or Slack.app. Up to 160 characters after trimming; longer values mark the row invalid.

bundle_id.description: CFBundleIdentifier, such as com.tinyspeck.slackmacgap. Matched before the name. Up to 255 characters after trimming; longer values mark the row invalid.

version.description: Installed CFBundleShortVersionString, as a string. Up to 80 characters after trimming; longer values mark the row invalid.

build.description: Installed CFBundleVersion, as a string. Up to 80 characters after trimming; longer values mark the row invalid.

publisher.description: Publisher or vendor name. Used only to group rows that have no bundle ID. Up to 160 characters after trimming; longer values mark the row invalid.

csv.description: Delimited export text. Recognized raw formats support 1 MiB and 5000 rows. App-only CSV or TSV supports 250 rows and 64 KiB. Mutually exclusive with rows and json.

json.description: Jamf Pro inventory or system_profiler export as JSON text, an object, or an array. Maximum 1 MiB and 5000 rows. Mutually exclusive with rows and csv.

format.description: Raw export profile for csv or json. Omission enables detection from the export headers or JSON shape.

target_macos.description: macOS major version to assess, 26, 27 or 28. 28 is the first release without general-purpose Rosetta 2. Omit for architecture evidence only.

filter.description: Return only rows with this status. Defaults to all. Counts always cover the whole batch.

offset.description: Number of filtered unique rows to skip. Defaults to 0. Maximum 249 for app-only input and 4999 for raw exports. next_offset refers to the same input, target_macos, filter and catalog_revision.

limit.description: Maximum rows per page, from 1 to 50. Defaults to 20.

catalog_revision.description: catalog_revision from the first page. A changed catalog returns an error so pages are not mixed across revisions.
